decision_a.overall_risk_rationale: Occupancy (−29.9%) and RevPAR (−31.5%) have declined substantially in the last month, which creates a meaningful revenue risk for a small 36‑room, 2‑star hotel. Offsetting this, guest satisfaction is rising (average rating +7.7%) and many recent reviews are strongly positive. The combination suggests an operational/marketing response is needed rather than an immediate reputational crisis.
decision_a.executive_summary: Priority actions: (1) arrest the drop in occupancy/RevPAR through targeted pricing and distribution/marketing moves; (2) resolve room comfort defects (mattresses, pillows) that reduce repeat business and value perception; (3) repair bathroom/shower issues now (safety risk); (4) optimise room layouts and remove obstructions to improve perceived space; (5) protect and promote strong service, cleanliness and breakfast to support recovery. Immediate maintenance on showers and a short-term pricing/marketing plan are the highest priorities.

priorities.problem: Occupancy fell from ~34.5% to ~24.2% (−29.9%) and RevPAR fell ~31.5% over the lookback. This threatens near-term revenue for a small property.
priorities.recommended_action: Conduct a brief diagnostic of booking sources and rate competitiveness; implement short-term tactical actions (temporary targeted discounts or packages for nearby markets, promote free parking and family rooms, weekend/family packages, ensure OTA visibility and accurate descriptions). Run a 4–8 week promotion targeted to the hotel’s common guest origins (Spain/Portugal) and family segments while monitoring conversion. If channel mix shows reliance on low-yield sources, adjust distribution strategy.
priorities.rationale: Large revenue/occupancy declines require fast commercial response; recent reviews show strengths (staff, breakfast, parking, family orientation) that can be highlighted in promotions to rebuild demand.

priorities.problem: Guests reported a sunken mattress and very thin pillows which reduce comfort and perceived value (explicit complaints about mattress needing replacement and thin pillows).
priorities.recommended_action: Inspect mattresses and pillows across all rooms immediately to identify worst-condition units. Create a prioritized replacement plan (replace worst mattresses first), standardize pillow options (offer firmer/softer alternatives), and record condition in maintenance log. Budget for phased mattress replacement if full replacement is unaffordable immediately.
priorities.rationale: Comfort items like mattresses and pillows have a direct effect on guest satisfaction and repeat bookings; targeted investment will improve reviews and help revenue recovery.
supporting_evidence: Review: "The mattress needs replacing, it's very sunken."

priorities.problem: At least one guest reported the handheld shower wasn't working properly; malfunctioning showers can reduce satisfaction and present scalding/slip risks if water flow or temperature control is inconsistent.
priorities.recommended_action: Order immediate inspection and repair of bathroom fixtures (handheld showers and mixers). Test water temperature stability and flow in all rooms, replace faulty hoses/heads/mixers as needed, and add the checks to a room maintenance checklist. Log repairs and confirm fixes with a short post‑repair test by staff.
priorities.rationale: Plumbing failures are straightforward to fix but can have safety implications and strongly negative impression if left unaddressed; fixing them quickly reduces risk and improves guest experience.
supporting_evidence: Review: "the handheld shower wasn't working properly."
Other reviews reference hot shower and bathtub (shows guests value functioning showers).

priorities.problem: A guest reported the room was very tight and you almost have to move the chair to get to the bathroom, indicating suboptimal furniture layout or oversized furniture in some rooms.
priorities.recommended_action: Survey room layouts to identify units with constrained circulation. Reconfigure or remove bulky/unused furniture (e.g., heavy chairs or tables) to improve access to the bathroom. Update room photos and descriptions to set correct expectations for small rooms, and consider lightweight/space-saving furniture on next replacement cycle.
priorities.rationale: Small changes to furniture and presentation can materially improve perceived room comfort without major capital outlay and reduce guest friction points.
supporting_evidence: Review: "The room was very tight; you almost have to move the chair to get to the bathroom."

priorities.area: Preserve and promote breakfast & service strengths

priorities.recommended_action: Maintain breakfast quality and staff service standards. Consider small, low-cost breakfast enhancements (e.g., one additional hot item or local speciality) and train/recognize staff to sustain the personable service noted by guests. Use positive guest comments about staff, cleanliness, free parking and family support in marketing messages.
priorities.rationale: Positive guest experience elements are already driving good ratings; protecting and modestly improving them supports occupancy recovery and guest loyalty.

decision_b.overall_risk_rationale: Business indicators show meaningful declines (REVPAR, occupancy, sentiment) and a consistent increase in operational complaints. Customer reviews nevertheless show clear strengths (cleanliness, friendly staff, satisfactory breakfast and parking). The combination of declining commercial metrics and emerging operational friction (bathroom/shower issues, mattress/room comfort expectation violations) warrants active managerial attention but does not indicate an immediate safety crisis.
decision_b.executive_summary: Preserve strong housekeeping and service performance while addressing a small set of operational/maintenance frictions that are beginning to affect guest expectations: (1) bathroom/shower functionality and layout obstructions (emerging); (2) room comfort (mattress condition and perceived cramped layouts); (3) rising operational complaints (process/reliability review); (4) expectation alignment on price–value messaging. Also monitor declining commercial metrics (RevPAR, occupancy, sentiment) to see whether guest experience issues are contributing. Prioritize assessment where capital or structural action may be required; otherwise pursue operational and policy/process fixes in the short term.

priorities.area: Room comfort (mattress condition and compact room layouts)
priorities.problem: Guest-reported mattress sagging (sunken mattress) and recurring comments about limited room space for some configurations (e.g., three-person room, moving furniture to access bathroom).
priorities.recommended_action: Conduct a targeted inspection program to assess mattress condition across room types and evaluate whether mattress replacement is warranted. Review room layouts/room type assignments (e.g., three-person configurations) and in-room furniture placement standards to reduce access friction. If inspections indicate widespread mattress deterioration or structural layout constraints, develop a replacement or refit plan (start with most-complained rooms).
